chapter: Postwar: Chicago, Vinson, Hines and Cootie
title: Sid Catlett and 52nd Street
summary: Gus talks about meeting Sid Catlett, who received him kindly, and about the Onyx Club and Famous Door on 52nd Street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, listen, we haven't talked about them. We should talk about them in a way. When did you know
Sid Catlett?
I met him in New York, at the --
Did you enjoy him?
Oh, yes. He was real cool with his brush work, too, you see.
He was a very fine drummer.
Oh, yes, he was. I'm telling you.
And a nice guy.
He certainly was. He received me just like I received him. I was very happy to meet him, and he acted the same way, like he was happy to meet me.
Yeah, very nice.
And I was nothing in his eyes, to me.
I'm a little old guy from Kansas City.
A Western dog.
Yeah, a little Western dog, as he said. But he received me just like he'd been knowing me a long time.
That's very nice. He'd heard you play.
And he --
That's very, very nice.
And every time I'd go down to the Onyx Club, he was playing with -- it was Stuff Smith.
Well, Cozy was with Stuff. Was he?
Yeah, but he was playing with Stuff Smith also.
Was he?
And John --
Kirby.
Not John Kirby, no. This is --
What did he play?
Bass.
Oh.
John Levy.
Oh, yes, of course.
John Levy was playing bass.
Yeah, oh.
And I think Jones was playing piano. Not Hank Jones. Jimmy Jones, he was playing piano.
Oh, he was? So it was Jimmy Jones and John Levy and Sid --
Sid and Stuff Smith.
Oh, is that right? That was before he and Jonah and Cozy went into the Famous Door, I guess. Because you said the Onyx Club, didn't you?
Yeah, I said the Onyx Club.
So that was before, I guess.
Yeah, and the Famous Door, that was on --
52nd.
52nd Street, yeah.
So was the Onyx.
Yeah, the Onyx was right across the street, see.
Yeah.
And Three Deuces was right in front of the Onyx Club.
Yeah, that's right. Well, that was nice, that was very --
